about: Timeline sort pairs never dealt together (design §4.5): every event in a against every event in b, because their order is honestly disputed. The build fails if windows or facts would settle one.

contested.reason: The Hebrew text of Genesis 5 has Enoch taken 69 years before Noah was born; the Samaritan text's smaller ages at fatherhood put Noah's birth about 180 years before Enoch was taken.
Genesis does not say how long after the Flood Noah planted his vineyard (he lived 350 years after it, Genesis 9:28), so its time against Babel and Terah's move is not stated.

Ezra 7:7's 'seventh year of Artaxerxes' is 458 BC (Artaxerxes I, the traditional view) or 398 BC (Artaxerxes II, held by many scholars since van Hoonacker); Nehemiah came in Artaxerxes I's twentieth year, 445/444 BC, and returned after his thirty-second, 433/432 BC.

Judges 17–21 is set early (Phinehas, Aaron's grandson, is priest, Judges 20:28) but is not tied to any judge, so its order against each judge's story is unknown. Othniel is included because nothing orders the war against him either.
Ruth's story is set 'in the days when the judges ruled' (Ruth 1:1), but under which judge is not said; Eli and Samuel were judges too (1 Samuel 4:18; 7:15).
Both fall in the first years after Babylon fell; Daniel 6:28 names the reigns of Darius and Cyrus without ordering these events, and who 'Darius the Mede' was is itself debated.
Luke has the family go home to Nazareth after the presentation (Luke 2:39); Matthew has the wise men's visit and the flight to Egypt. How the two accounts fit together is debated.
The Gospels arrange Galilean events differently, and neither event is tied in time to the other.
